html:
The Polish Round Table Talks were negotiations held in Warsaw from February to April 1989 between the communist government and the opposition led by Solidarity, which agreed to partly free elections.

Strikes in 1988 and an economy in ruins pushed the government to talk. The deal made Solidarity legal again and set elections in which all seats in a new Senate and a third of the seats in the lower house were open. On 4 June 1989 Solidarity won all but one of the seats it could contest. In August Tadeusz Mazowiecki became the first non communist prime minister in the Soviet bloc. Lech Wałęsa was elected president in 1990. The Polish example set off the revolutions of 1989 across eastern Europe, and Poland joined NATO in 1999 and the EU in 2004.
sum: The Polish Round Table Talks were negotiations held in Warsaw from February to April 1989 between the communist government and the opposition led by Solidarity, which agreed to partly free elections.
